 New OTT releases to watch this week: 9 new movies and shows on Netflix, JioHotstar, Prime Video, ZEE5 and more
 SECTIONS New OTT releases to watch this week: 9 new movies and shows on Netflix, JioHotstar, Prime Video, ZEE5 and more By ET Entertainment Desk , ET Online Last Updated: Oct 27, 2026, 08:52:00 AM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis This week, from October 26 to November 1, OTT platforms will release several exciting new movies and shows across different genres, including action-comedy, family drama, and horror. Featured titles will be Baththa, Akka, and The One About Matthew Perry, along with Minimum Wage and Obsession. This diverse lineup promises something for everyone looking to explore fresh content. Read on!
 OTT releases of the week (Credit: Instagram) From a supernatural wish that takes a disturbing turn to a crime investigation involving a dangerous serial killer, this week’s OTT lineup has plenty to explore. Viewers can also look forward to a Diwali family drama, a documentary about a beloved Friends star and a comedy set inside a struggling pizza shop. With new titles arriving between October 26 and November 1, here are nine movies and shows to add to your watchlist.
 Baththa - Netflix 
Vijay Sethupathi returns with Baththa, a Tamil action-comedy that mixes gangster drama with humour. Directed by Balaji Tharaneetharan, the film also stars Lijomol Jose and Sai Prithviraj. Baththa will premiere on Netflix on October 29, 2026. Along with Tamil, the film will be available in dubbed versions in Telugu, Hindi, Kannada and Malayalam. 
 Akka - Netflix 
Akka takes place in a fictional kingdom where women have ruled for generations. Set in the 1980s, the series takes place in Pernuru, where the arrival of a new figure threatens the existing balance of power. Keerthy Suresh plays Bhavani, while Radhika Apte appears as Rudra, whose arrival sets the conflict in motion. Featuring Tanvi Azmi, Mahesh Manjrekar, Anshuman Pushkar and Monica Panwar, the series is written and directed by Dharmaraj Shetty and produced by YRF Entertainment. Akka arrives on Netflix on October 30.

 The One About Matthew Perry - Netflix 
 Fans of Friends can revisit the life and career of Matthew Perry through a three-part documentary about the actor best known for playing Chandler Bing. Directed by Mary Robertson, The One About Matthew Perry features accounts from his family, friends and colleagues, alongside previously unreleased photographs and videos. It looks at his rise to fame, his struggles with addiction and his efforts to support others facing similar challenges. The documentary premieres on Netflix on October 27.
 Meethe Mein Kya Hai - Netflix

In this upcoming Hindi family drama, relatives come together for the festival of Diwali and the celebrations turn emotional. The gathering brings family members under one roof, but also brings unresolved disagreements and differences between generations to the fore. Ritwik Bhowmik and Rohini Hattangadi lead the cast, with Ayesha Raza and Gaurav Sharma also featuring in the film. The family drama will be available on Netflix from October 30.
 Sigma - Netflix 
Sundeep Kishan headlines Sigma, a Tamil action drama that marks Jason Sanjay’s directorial debut. Jason is the son of Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay. The film also features Faria Abdullah, Raju Sundaram, Sampath Raj and Shiv Panditt in significant roles. Thaman has composed the music, and Lyca Productions has backed the project. Sigma makes its OTT debut on Netflix on October 30, with multiple language options, including Telugu and Hindi.
 Minimum Wage - Netflix 
A small-town pizza shop becomes the setting for workplace chaos in Minimum Wage. Starring Grace Reiter and Randall Park, the comedy uses a mockumentary format to follow teenage employees dealing with demanding customers, a struggling valet service and an absent boss. Things become more complicated when the boss returns and expects the business to turn profitable. With episodes running for approximately 12 minutes, the series is a short-form option for viewers. It starts streaming on Netflix on October 26.
 Obsession - JioHotstar 
What happens when a wish for love turns into a nightmare? Directed by Curry Barker, the horror film Obsession follows Bear, played by Michael Johnston, who uses a supernatural object called the One Wish Willow to make his childhood friend Nikki fall in love with him. However, Nikki, played by Inde Navarrette, becoming the object of his wish sets off a frightening chain of events. The original uncut version will stream in English and Hindi on JioHotstar’s Peacock Hub from October 30.
 Nocturne - Apple TV 
A murder investigation leads into the disturbing world of a serial killer in Nocturne. Liev Schreiber plays homicide detective Jonah Lynn, whose case is connected to Jurek Walter, portrayed by Stephen Graham. Meanwhile, Zazie Beetz plays FBI agent Saga Bauer, who goes undercover to seek answers. Based on Lars Kepler’s crime novels The Sandman and The Lazarus, the 10-episode thriller begins with two episodes on Apple TV on October 30. New episodes will follow weekly until December 25. The supporting cast includes Bill Camp, Rory Culkin, Chrissy Metz and Gary Carr.
 Apocalypse Z: New World - Prime Video 
The fight for survival continues in Apocalypse Z: New World, the sequel to Apocalypse Z: The Beginning of the End. The story returns to a world devastated by the TSJ virus, which transforms people into dangerous infected creatures. Directed by Carles Torrens, the film explores the risks survivors face as they figure out the infected world and decide whom they can trust. Berta Vazquez returns as Lucía, while Jose María Yazpik reprises his role as Pritchenko. Tamara Casellas and Mario Mayo also feature in the film, which arrives on Prime Video on October 30.
